notes: Rows are now calibrated to the four MEASURED suspension-row anchors rather than picked. Three candidate models were tested against them: cosine of body angle (RMSE 0.024), linear in angle from vertical (RMSE 0.011, best), and a lever-about-the-feet model which was REJECTED because it predicts a constant load. Per-anchor residuals are in the source beside the numbers. Upright 0.38, reference 0.57, horizontal 0.81

Two families were borrowing geometry that was not theirs. A hanging leg raise is HIP flexion, not trunk flexion, so it no longer takes the crunch 0.40: both legs are 0.322 of bodyweight with a mean cosine of 0.64 over the sweep, giving 0.21 straight-leg and 0.15 bent-knee. Nordic and glute-ham were both 0.70 and are now split at 0.68 and 0.59 from upper-body mass at the knee lever

Two rules were UNREACHABLE and silently did nothing: the razor curl factor was never gated on, and an Australian pull-up was being shadowed by the pull-up pattern and scored as a full hanging pull-up at 1.00. Both fixed. Plank stays 0.00 on purpose: a hold moves nothing, so any non-zero factor would manufacture tonnage and a 1RM out of a static pose.
